headline: High-risk default interaction: Claude Code can read/write shared files and run shell/MCP, while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list with no protective surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject Claude Code. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or files the operator places into Claude Code’s workspace, which makes the pathway unusual and limited. Claude Code’s file and stdin/stdout surfaces make it the more exposed side.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies content from awesome-nlp into Claude Code prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF Claude Code is pointed at a workspace containing attacker-controlled text, it may parse that text as instructions.
mitigations: Avoid copying untrusted list entries into prompts.
Keep Claude Code in a separate workspace from reference material.
Use a read-only notes file for pasted content.
Review any pasted text before sending.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported snippets.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has no runtime, so it is not a meaningful source of leakage. Claude Code does handle files, git history, shell environment, and secrets, but the pair itself does not create a shared workspace by default. Leakage risk mainly appears if the operator places sensitive files from Claude Code into a shared directory or pastes them into the list context.
conditions: IF Claude Code is run in a directory containing secrets or private source code, those files can be read by the agent.
IF the operator copies sensitive content from Claude Code into shared notes or issue trackers, it can leak externally.
mitigations: Run Claude Code in a minimal working directory.
Remove secrets from the workspace before use.
Keep reference lists and project files in separate folders.
Audit pasted content before sharing externally.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with separate mounts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write, shell, git, or network capabilities, so it cannot conflict over mutable resources with Claude Code. Claude Code can modify files and git state, but there is no second active writer in the pair. The interaction is therefore not a capability conflict.
conditions: IF a separate writable agent is added to the same directory, write conflicts could emerge.
IF the operator manually edits the same files while Claude Code runs, local conflicts may occur.
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp as a static reference only.
Avoid concurrent manual edits in Claude Code worktrees.
Use git branches for Claude Code changes.
Commit frequently to reduce merge ambiguity.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a static curated list, not an action-taking agent, so Claude Code is unlikely to treat its output as authoritative machine-generated facts. Still, if the operator uses entries from the list as instructions or code sources without verification, Claude Code could propagate mistakes into files or commits. The blast radius is limited to the user’s workspace.
conditions: IF the operator asks Claude Code to implement code copied from awesome-nlp entries without checking provenance, errors can cascade into commits.
IF Claude Code is instructed to trust pasted list content as authoritative, it may act on incorrect guidance.
mitigations: Verify any copied recommendations before acting on them.
Ask Claude Code to summarize rather than execute pasted guidance.
Review diffs before commit.
Keep source links alongside copied snippets.
requires-engineering: add citation/provenance checks to downstream workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, so only Claude Code’s documented handling of local files and git history is relevant. Because the other agent is a static open-source list, it does not itself introduce a compliance boundary. Risk arises only if regulated data is placed into Claude Code’s workspace or logs.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the Claude Code workspace, it may be processed outside the intended compliance boundary.
IF the operator uses Claude Code on data subject to stricter retention rules than the local repo, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace.
Use a sanitized sample repository.
Review local retention and logging settings.
Keep compliance-sensitive files in a separate protected location.
requires-engineering: document approved data classes for Claude Code use.
